Independent quadratic quotient reduction and cubic sign check
correctness.rationale: On the hub/common-ordinary/exceptional quotient M the nonzero eigenvalues solve lambda^2-a lambda+b=0, with a=k+1+2x and b=(k+2)x; the ordinary-leaf differences have eigenvalue 1. Write Delta for the product of the two positive scalar denominators at the nonzero eigenvalues. On the quotient the rational update is I-12h[(12+6ha+h^2(a^2-b))M-(6h+ah^2)M^2]/Delta: the linear factor in the numerator comes from the denominator evaluated at the other nonzero eigenvalue. Taking entries and subtracting the scalar leaf-difference contribution reproduces p, r, the strictly positive ordinary-to-exceptional entry and the cubic q. The scalar numerator is (z-3)^2+3, so the diagonal entries are positive. The unique positive roots of p and r in their respective ranges give the stated radicals. The cubic's first three coefficients in ascending order are positive; a negative cubic coefficient occurs exactly for x<1/(k+4) and gives a unique positive zero. Reducing q at the positive root of p by h^2=(12+6xh)/(x(1-2x)) gives the stated strictly positive remainder, so the second zero is later. Alternatively the general resolvent sign specializes to a strictly decreasing scalar for the ordinary pair, recorded below. This verifies that the full positivity set includes h=0 and the finite cutoffs, and that there is no reentry.
residual_risks: The observed 2886 scripted checks recorded in the package are not a new execution or a proof by finite samples.
The result concerns exact completed steps, not positivity of internal stages or numerical-roundoff guarantees.

evidence: For distinct leaves the sign is the sign of Im(1/F_ij), with 1/F_ij=(s+w_i)(s+w_j) Omega(s)/(w_i w_j), Omega(s)=1+sum w_j/(s+w_j), s=(3+i sqrt(3))/h.
For the ordinary pair this is (s+1)^2+k(s+1)+x(s+1)^2/(s+x). Polynomial division gives Im(1/F_ij)/Im(s)=k+2+x+6/h-x(1-x)^2 h^2/d(xh).
claim_vs_prior_implication.reasoning: This scalar is strictly decreasing on h>0 since 6/h is and h^2/d(xh) is strictly increasing; it starts at +infinity and tends to k+4-1/x. It is positive at every finite h for a nonnegative limit, and has one root followed by negativity exactly for x<1/(k+4). The general theorem already makes every leaf pair strictly positive at the first horizon, placing this secondary root strictly later. Multiplying the scalar by h d(xh) reproduces q. Thus the subsidiary claim is an exact elementary implication of the same indexed source, not merely a speculative overlap.

evidence: The all-weight theorem tests Phi_*=1-sum_j h^2 w_j(w_*-w_j)/d(hw_j), d(z)=z^2+6z+12, with a unique root in the finite-horizon case.
The criterion for unconditional positivity is w_* sum_j(1/w_j)<=m+1; precisely the maximum-spoke hub entries vanish at a finite threshold.
equivalent_formulations.reasoning: Take m=k+1, w=(1,...,1,x). For x<=1 the unconditional criterion becomes k+1/x<=k+2, and Phi_*=p(h)/d(xh). For x>=1 it becomes kx+1<=k+2, and Phi_*=r(h)/d(h). The closed interval and both radical horizons follow from those quadratics; the controlling entries are exactly the maximum spokes.

originality.rationale: An indexed theorem on all positively weighted stars gives the entire nonnegative timestep set and first failing entries for this family. Its exact off-diagonal resolvent identity also reduces immediately to a monotone scalar whose limit is k+4-1/x, mechanically giving the secondary threshold and all signs on either side. Neither the radical expressions nor the apparently additional ordinary-pair transition survive the exact comparison. This establishes coverage, not derivational priority.

value.rationale: A single exceptional spoke is a natural symmetry-breaking test and the order of sign failures is useful. Here both the sharp horizon and the later leaf-pair sign follow directly from the exact all-star resolvent; the radical roots and the secondary cutoff only evaluate that formula for a special set of weights. No independent scientific remainder justifies a narrowed repair.
residual_risks: The specialized formulas can be convenient for exposition, which is separate from scientific value as a distinct result.
